original_question: In a domain with smooth boundary in Euclidean space, fix a generic interior point P and consider the time-t front consisting of light rays emitted from P in all directions, reflected specularly at the boundary, and evolved for time t. Does this time-t front become dense as t tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, open problem "Density of reflected wave fronts".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim: a domain with smooth boundary in Euclidean space, a generic interior point P, light rays emitted from P in all directions, specular/optical reflections at the boundary, the time-t front, and the question of whether that front becomes dense as t tends to infinity.
missing_details: The ambient set in which density is asked should be stated explicitly: the front is meant to become dense in the billiard domain Ω itself.
For a stand-alone formulation, the time-t front should be defined as a set F_t of endpoints at time t of all unit-speed billiard trajectories starting at P.
The reflection law should be identified explicitly as the usual optical/specular billiard reflection law at hits with ∂Ω.
The paper leaves "generic point" informal; if one wants a fully stand-alone statement, one should either preserve that informality or separately specify the genericity notion.

The paper does not formalize "become dense" in 2602.12896; for a fully stand-alone version one should state what asymptotic density means for the family F_t, e.g. eventual intersection with every nonempty open subset of Ω.
This is posed in the paper as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture with additional hypotheses such as convexity, boundedness, or dimension restrictions.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ R^n be a domain with smooth boundary, and let P ∈ Ω be a generic interior point. For each t ≥ 0, let F_t ⊂ Ω be the time-t wave front, namely the set of endpoints at time t of all unit-speed rays starting at P in every initial direction and reflecting from ∂Ω according to the usual optical/specular billiard law. Is it true that F_t becomes dense in Ω as t → ∞, in the sense that every nonempty open subset of Ω intersects F_t for all sufficiently large t?
justification: The draft clearly targets the Serge Tabachnikov open problem titled "Density of reflected wave fronts," not any numbered Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 elsewhere in the paper. The wording of your draft is already extremely close to the paper's own formulation. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to make the moving set F_t explicit and to specify that density is being asked inside the domain Ω. I did not add convexity, boundedness, dimension restrictions, or a Riemannian generalization, because the paper does not add them here. The nearby context only adds that the corresponding problem for smooth Riemannian manifolds is discussed in reference [79], and that even the round circle case is open.
